subject: Using an offset in pformula in pcountOpen?

messages.author: f4bebbdb3c5fcabc
messages.subject: Using an offset in pformula in pcountOpen?
parts:
I have been working with unmarked for a while now, but have run into something I haven't been able to find an answer to.


Let me start off by saying that I am working with data which was not collected with occupancy/abundance modeling in mind. Basically this is an exercise in figuring out if this type of modeling can give us some useful answers in terms of trends, since the data is zero-inflated. I have count data for a species for a number of years, and there are a number of surveys per year. I am using pcountOpen and am using the year as the primary sampling period.

However, within the year, the area sampled at a site is not always the same. So for instance in Feb a larger area was sampled than in June. The area is recorded, so I reckoned it’s possible to use it as an offset (essentially, if you use the number given for the sampled area, you divide the count of individuals by that number, you get number of individuals per 100m2). 


So in terms of adding the offset, in most explanations I have seen, the area just differs between sites - not between surveys - so the offset is added to the abundance probability distribution function (lambda formula). So this would give you individuals per 100m2. But, in our case, the area also differs per observation (survey).


In our case, could we add it to the detection probability distribution function, as the area size is essentially an observation-level covariate? I guess?

Would the interpretation then be the probability of detection per 100m2? Can we still interpret abundance as individuals per 100m2 then (as would be the case if we added an offset there)?


I don't really want to add the area as an actual covariate, as I feel it might eclipse other covariates (in p-values). I'd rather just control for area. But maybe that would make more sense? 


I am trying to wrap my head around this conceptually, but not sure if I'm getting it right - I haven't worked with offsets much.


Thanks!

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Using an offset in pformula in pcountOpen?
parts:
Do you have two different "areas" ?  One that is constant for a site across all surveys (associated with abundance) and another that is the survey area (a subset of the site area) which varies among surveys (associated with detection)?  If including site area for the abundance model affects the selection of other covariates, doesn't that suggest caution in interpreting the effect of covariates if site area is not considered in a suite of models to be examined?

Jim

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Using an offset in pformula in pcountOpen?
parts:
Thanks Jim, and apologies for only getting back to this now. I got side-tracked by some other things, but also spent quite some time trying to think through this, and trying to figure out if I understand your response - I think I do now.

Yes, you do have a good point there. Leaving the areas out of the detection probability formula was probably too hasty. I am rerunning things with area included in the detection probability estimation.

I am trying to think through what that means for the interpretation of the abundance results. The area numbers are all scaled to 100 m^2, i.e. if you took the counts of the animals and divided it by the area number, you'd get animals per 100 m^2 (density).
For my estimating my model, I standardize all variables. So I guess any linkage with the 100 m^2 goes lost there.

So my thinking is now that I can't really say anything about densities, but rather only numbers at a site (similar to counting bird calls, where one does not really know how large an area is covered).

Any thoughts on this?
